# SPD-065 — Refactor bin/spud_ledger.py (10663 lines) into a package of ~250-line modules: Phase 1 extraction plan, Phase 2 implementation

## Brief
Eric's ask (2026-09-15, the Spud half; BAD-036 is the BadTakes half, running in its own session): before any further feature work, refactor every application code file over 1000 lines into modules of a size that can be held and worked on concurrently, to make concurrent work and maintenance tractable. Two phases. Phase 1 is planning only: analyze the file's responsibilities (types, business logic and state, helper utilities, sub-components), propose a directory and file structure, list every planned new file and exactly what moves into it, and guarantee the original entry point keeps the exact same public surface so nothing that loads or imports it breaks. Eric approves the file layout before any code is written. Phase 2 is implementation, in this order: shared types and pure utilities first, then state and services, then sub-components, then the entry file reduced to an orchestrator; verified with zero behaviour change.

Eric's clarification (2026-09-15, 10:40): ~250 lines is not a hard cap. It is the point at which a module is worth a second look; a module may be as large as it needs to be, and the larger it gets the more it must justify itself. No cohesive function, class or region is cut to fit a number. Scope is application code only (Python, Node and the like); stylesheets, HTML and test files are out.

Survey at the ticket's creation, tracked application code files at or over 1000 lines:

| File | Lines | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bin/spud_ledger.py | 10663 | the ledger program: CLI, render, import, projects, sessions and all eight hooks, in one module, 664 top-level symbols; loaded by the launcher bin/spud with bytecode cached under the state directory's pycache |

bin/spud, the launcher, is 55 lines and stays. tests/test_hooks.py (4888 lines) is a test file and out of scope by Eric's clarification.

Constraints every plan must honour, from CLAUDE.md, the launcher and the program's own header:
- `bin/spud` stays the one program that writes the ledger and the one path the hooks, the allow rules, `settings sync` and `project install` name. It runs under `python3.14 -I -S` (isolated, no site, standard library only, nothing on sys.path but the interpreter's own), so a package beside it is not importable by name: the launcher loads the program by file path with SourceFileLoader, and every module of a split must be found the same way, never through the working directory or sys.path.
- Bytecode: the launcher caches the program's bytecode under the home's state directory (`<home>/.spud/pycache/`) in a tree mirroring the program's own path, so a worktree's program and the main checkout's never share a file, and it writes nothing unless that directory exists; the test suite asserts the repo is left with no bytecode. Compiling the one module cost a hook run 25 of its 65 ms (SPD-016); a split into many modules compiled on every hook run would be worse, so the plan must say how every module's bytecode is cached there and how the edit hook's refusal of that directory still covers it.
- Hook latency: every Bash, Edit and Agent call runs `spud hook PreToolUse`; SessionStart, Stop, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, PostToolUse and UserPromptSubmit too. The LazyModule pattern defers argparse, subprocess, hashlib, tempfile and fractions because importing them cost every hook run 11 ms. The split must keep the hook path's import set minimal (render, import, cost, projects, schedule and the parser imported only by the commands that need them) and measure the hook run before and after.
- The program run directly refuses; keep that.
- Public surface: tests/helpers.py loads bin/spud_ledger.py as module `spud_ledger` via SourceFileLoader and the suite (702 tests) reaches its symbols by attribute, including monkeypatching module globals such as `now`, `run_git` and the environment readers at their call sites. A name moved into a submodule and imported by value into another module no longer patches at the call site. The plan must enumerate every symbol the suite and the launcher touch, and make the compatibility argument per symbol: either the entry module re-exports it and call sites look it up through the module that defines it, or the test changes are listed explicitly as part of the ticket (a mechanical rename of the attribute path is acceptable if listed; behaviour change is not).
- Hook self-recognition: the Bash hook vouches for calls of the launcher (`spud_launcher`, `any_spud_launcher`, `launcher_vouched`, `spud_home_vouched`, `interpreter_vouched`) and the edit hook refuses the state directory that holds the hook bytecode; `git_binary_fingerprint` and `worktrees_fingerprint` cache on file identity. The plan must show these keep working when the program is a package, in the main checkout and in every worktree.
- One file, one worktree, one branch, one merge: the split lands as a single ticket on main, because a half-split program cannot be hooked into a session. Phase 2 sequencing inside the branch follows Eric's order.
- Verification is the suite: `python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` (702 tests, about seven minutes), plus a hook-run timing before and after, plus the headless probes under tests/probes/ where they apply.
- CLAUDE.md names bin/spud_ledger.py in two places (the ledger CLI paragraph and Commands); the plan lists the lines that change, Spud edits them.

Phase 1 plan: one architect spudagent (fable) writes the spike at the Spud home under docs/spikes/spd-065/spud-ledger.md, with the responsibility map, the proposed tree, the per-file move list (every top-level symbol assigned to exactly one module, with line counts), the entry-point and test-suite compatibility argument, the loader and bytecode-cache design, the hook-latency argument, the verification recipe, and every module over ~250 lines with the reason it is right to leave it whole (cmd_ledger_commit, build_parser, ShellWalk, analyse_words are candidates). Spud then presents the layout to Eric; Phase 2 activates as one worktree and one merge once he approves.

## Size, persona and model decision
Phase 1: one architect on fable writing the spike, with up to two children (scouts on haiku for symbol and test-reference surveys, or an architect on fable for the hook region) if the file is too big to hold; Phase 2, after Eric approves: one engineer on opus in one worktree, a reviewer on fable before the merge. Line size: ~250 is the look-again point, not a cap (Eric, 2026-09-15).
